source_dispositions.decision: All four transformations retained through the complete net RHEA:45145; no duplicate net plus component edges. The primary assigns hydration/hydrolysis to DmdD, spontaneous MeSH elimination and expected spontaneous decarboxylation.
Its word reduction for MMPA-CoA to MTA-CoA conflicts with the native sides, loss of two hydrogen atoms and primary oxidation evidence. Use oxidation, retain original contradictory prose here.
Retain generic database carrier-class convention with explicit uncertainty; direct primary evidence used artificial acceptors and does not identify an exact physiological ETF.

Native catalyst projection uses DmdB2/SPO2045, DmdC1/SPO3804 and DmdD/SPO3805. Other DSS-3 DmdB/DmdC isozymes are acknowledged alternatives, not silently declared absent or assigned the selected proteins their distinct regulatory/acceptor properties.

Detailed DmdB structure is from R. lacuscaerulensis ITI-1157 and DmdC structure/ free-FAD activity from R. nubinhibens ISM. Retained as cross-species context, not direct DSS-3 structural or electron-acceptor proof.

source_dispositions.decision: Retain directly measured DMSP inhibition and isozyme-specific MMPA relief. High-concentration nonspecific salt effects and proposed transcription/metabolic feedback loops do not become regulator or physiological activation edges.
No compartment node or localization edge is asserted from unspecified purification or family context.

Direct dimer/dimer/hexamer evidence remains on qualified functional enables edges. Native MONOMER frame names are gene-product identifiers, not evidence of monomer sufficiency; no invented complex identifier.
DmdA-mediated DMSP demethylation precedes PWY-6048; acetaldehyde oxidation and methanethiol assimilation follow it and remain outside this exact route.
Current inventory has no Ruegeria dataset; root applicability receipt applies, no surrogate E. coli expression evidence.
